beats.say: The four corners of your screen are the easiest pixels on it to hit. Almost every app wastes them.
In nineteen fifty four, an air force psychologist named Paul Fitts sat people down and had them tap between two metal plates, as fast as they could without missing.

visual.headline: The information capacity of the human motor system
visual.body: Subjects tapped alternately between two metal plates, as fast as accuracy allowed. Movement time proved predictable from just two variables: how far the hand travelled, and how wide the target was.

beats.say: What he found became Fitts's Law. The time to hit a target grows with the distance your hand has to travel, and shrinks as the target gets bigger.

visual.def: The time to hit a target grows with distance and shrinks with size.

beats.say: Don't take my word for it. Watch. Same hand, same distance, two targets. The big one lands in about seven hundred milliseconds. The small one takes over eleven hundred.
So you have three levers. Make the target bigger. Move it closer. Or, the one most designers forget, give it an edge to stop against.

visual.title: What makes a target easy
steps: Give it an edge to stop against

beats.say: Because your cursor cannot fly off the screen. Throw it at the top edge and it stops dead, right on the menu. That makes an edge, and especially a corner, a target of effectively infinite size.

visual.title: Menu welded to the screen edge
visual.note: The edge stops the cursor dead — no aiming required.

beats.say: Move that same menu a few pixels inside a window and the trick is gone. The identical throw sails straight past it, and now you have to drag the cursor back.

visual.title: The same menu, floating in a window
visual.note: No wall to catch it — the throw overshoots and must be corrected.

beats.say: On a phone, the target moves with your grip. Only about a third of a large screen is comfortable for one thumb. Everything above that arc is a stretch, or a second hand.

visual.title: One-handed reach
visual.note: Inside the arc: easy. Above it: a stretch.

beats.say: Which is why the platforms put a floor under it. Apple asks for forty four points, google for forty eight, because the average fingertip covers about forty five pixels.
Put it together and the fix is usually free. Same screen, same content. Bigger targets, real spacing, and the destructive button moved away from the safe one.

before.label: Before
before.caption: 12 px links, no spacing, Delete beside Save

after.label: After
after.caption: 44 px targets, clear gaps, Delete moved away

beats.say: The four corners are still the easiest pixels on your screen. Now you know what belongs there.
